lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Improve this question for a local topic: "Why is everything different?"

FEEDBACK
For example: "How have the shops in our main street changed since 1980?" It names the place, time and what to look for.

WATCH FOR
A question that is too wide, or that has only a yes or no answer, cannot guide an investigation.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Choose a topic you can study. Write eight possible questions, choose one main question and three smaller sub-questions, and explain why your main question is open and investigable.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.

Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Choose a topic you can study. Write eight possible questions, choose one main question and three smaller sub-questions, and explain why your main question is open and investigable. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Likely misconception: A question that is too wide, or that has only a yes or no answer, cannot guide an investigation. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

teach_steps.explain:
An inquiry question is a focused question that can be answered using evidence from sources. Open questions often begin with how or why and need more than yes or no. An investigable question can be answered using people, places, objects, books or maps that you can reach.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the sources, map features or community examples that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a detail is uncertain, identify what source you would need next. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: A question that is too wide, or that has only a yes or no answer, cannot guide an investigation. Correct the claim or use of sources, not just the neatness of the poster.
